caption: A sheet of plastic wrap is torn from its box, and it clings to the side of the box and folds onto itself instead of hanging straight.

sa.check: A sheet of wrap is torn from the box.
The sheet clings to the side of the box.
The sheet folds onto itself and sticks there.
The wrap is thin and transparent.
The tear comes first and the clinging follows.

pc.expect: The torn sheet does not hang straight: it lies against the box's side where it touches and its folds stick to each other, staying so until pulled apart.
pc.fail: The sheet hangs straight down from the hand like paper and touches nothing; or a fold that touches the box falls away on its own; or folds that meet slide apart with nothing pulling them; or the sheet stands out stiff from the box.

pc.expect: The wrap is a thin limp film: it crumples, wrinkles and folds, stretches slightly when tugged, and peels off with a pull.
pc.fail: The wrap holds a flat rigid shape like a card; or drapes in heavy folds like cloth; or stretches out long like rubber and snaps back; or tears into shards like glass.

pc.expect: Parts of the sheet not stuck to anything hang downward; if the sheet is let go entirely it falls.
pc.fail: A free edge rises or stands out sideways with nothing near it; or the sheet floats when let go; or the sheet climbs up the box.

pc.expect: The box stays where it is while the sheet is torn and clings; the sheet moves only with the hand or as it settles onto the box.
pc.fail: The box slides or tips by itself; or the sheet crawls across the box after settling; or the sheet jumps between spots on the box with nothing touching it.

pc.expect: One sheet torn from one box; the sheet stays one piece and passes through nothing; the box keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The sheet splits into several pieces after the tear; or vanishes; or passes through the box; or the box changes shape or a second box appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The box's colours and lettering and the counter stay the same.
pc.fail: The box changes colour or lettering; or the counter changes; or the wrap changes colour.
